passages.note: Aye on Assembly concurrence in Senate amendments (final passage of the chaptered text); 16 of 77 voting were No, so not near-unanimous.

passages.provision_quote: shall not enact or enforce any policy, rule, or administrative regulation that would require an employee or a contractor to disclose any information related to a pupil’s sexual orientation, gender identity, or gender expression to any other person without the pupil’s consent, unless otherwise required by state or federal law.
passages.note: Chaptered text, which lists him as coauthor; Sec. 220.5 forbids rules that require disclosure, and Sec. 220.3 only frees staff from any requirement to disclose, so it does not require them to withhold (this rules out the rung-1 mandate).

rows.reasoning: Muratsuchi co-authored AB 1955 (2023-2024) and voted Aye on its final Assembly passage. Its operative Sec. 220.5 says schools "shall not enact or enforce any policy, rule, or administrative regulation that would require an employee or a contractor to disclose" a pupil's gender identity without consent, which matches "Forbid rules that require schools to tell parents." The bill does not require staff to keep the information from parents (it says only that they "shall not be required to disclose"), so the rung-1 mandate to keep it from parents is excluded.
